items.description: Google does not show all links, and not all spammy links, within the Search Console links report. This is not new, Google has long said that the link report only shows a sampling of links.

items.title: Google AI Overviews With Query Refinement Bubbles
items.description: Google is testing query refinement bubbles at the top of the AI Overviews in Google Search. But clicking the refinement bubble does not change the query, instead, it takes you into AI Mode for that query set.

items.title: Google AI Mode Tests Blending All Products With Sponsored Products
items.description: Google seems to be testing mixing sponsored products, ads, within the organic product results in AI Mode. Google has this line above the product results that can say "Sponsored" and "All products." Even as I look at screenshots of this, I am not sure if the "All products" are sponsored or not.

items.title: Google Merchant API With New October 2026 Updates
items.description: Google has released several updates to the Merchant API for October 26. The update expands YouTube Shopping and AI-commerce reporting, adds product attributes for videos and warranties, improves disapproval diagnostics, and introduces API integration enhancements and reporting deprecations.

items.title: Is Google Testing Dropping Citations Cards From AI Overviews?
items.description: Google may be testing removing the citations card on the Google AI Overviews section. So when you do a search on desktop and see an AI Overview, Google generally shows a citations card that has links to the sources you can click on. Google is reportedly testing removing that card from the interface.

items.title: Search Central Live India 2026: Bengaluru, We're Coming (For Real This Time)

In any case, you can finally stand up and stretch: Search Central Live is officially returning to India in 2026, specifically to Bengaluru!

items.title: Update to the Site Reputation Policy
items.description: In 2024, we introduced our site reputation policy to stop a practice where third-party content is published on a trusted website just to exploit that site's good reputation to rank higher in Search. This practice hurts search quality, and creates a bad experience for users.

items.title: Platform properties roll out globally, plus a new social and video performance guide

items.title: See how content from social and video platforms performs on Google Search

As people gravitate toward firsthand perspectives and different content formats, we want to make it easier for site owners and creators&mdash;even those without their own website&mdash;to get a consolidated view of how all of their content is getting discovered on Search.
